mainTopic: Whether a נזיר who is already impure gets new lashes for a second impurity or for entering a place with a dead body
overview: The גמרא brings two versions of what רב הונא said. In רבה's version, a נזיר gets separate lashes for becoming impure and for entering a place with a dead body, but not for becoming impure twice. רב יוסף swears that רב הונא held he is liable even for impurity after impurity, and he proves it from רב הונא's ruling about a נזיר in a cemetery. אביי objects from a ברייתא about a כהן already holding a dead body, and רב יוסף answers that our משנה makes a נזיר liable for each warning even though he is already impure. The גמרא settles the clash: the ברייתא is about someone still touching the first body, and the משנה is about someone who let go first. It then shows that direct contact with a body counts on a תורה level, unlike רבי ינאי's case of contact through another person. So impurity on top of impurity while still connected brings no new liability, just as רבה said. Finally, רבי יוחנן explains that entering brings separate lashes when a pure נזיר walks into a house, but not when he was already impure from a field.

steps.title: רבה's version of רב הונא: impurity and entering, but not impurity twice
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רב הונא: the verse "לא יטמא" covers every kind of impurity, and "לא יבא" adds a separate warning about entering, but a second impurity does not bring extra liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבה said in the name of רב הונא: The Torah wrote a full, clear verse, "He shall not become impure." So when it also says "He shall not come," it warns him about impurity and also warns him about entering. But for becoming impure and then becoming impure again, there is no separate warning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a statement by רב הונא, as reported by רבה, about how many sets of lashes a נזיר can get for corpse impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse "לא יטמא" already forbids every type of corpse impurity. So the extra phrase "לא יבא" is used to add a separate warning about entering a place with a dead body. However, if a נזיר who is already impure touches another dead body, that does not count as a new sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A full, clear verse that states the law openly
He shall not become impure: the נזיר's ban on corpse impurity
He shall not come: read here as a separate ban on entering where a dead body is
Entering a place where a dead body is
Becoming impure and then becoming impure again

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. "Impurity plus entering" brings two sets of lashes in this version, but "impurity plus impurity" brings only one.

phrases.english: Gemara
It was stated:
Rabba said that Rav Huna said:
The Torah spoke in a full, clear verse:
"He shall not become impure."
So when it says "He shall not come":
it warns him about impurity,
and warns him about entering.
But impurity and then impurity again: no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר is liable separately for impurity and for entering, but not for a second impurity on top of the first.

steps.title: רב יוסף's version: רב הונא said even impurity twice
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף swears that רב הונא actually said a נזיר is liable even for impurity on top of impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: By God! רב הונא said he is liable even for impurity and then impurity again.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different version of רב הונא's view, and he says it with an oath to show how sure he is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, רב הונא held that each new contact with a dead body is a new sin, even for someone who is already impure. This directly opposes the last line of רבה's version.

keyTerms.meaning: By God!: a strong oath expression
Even

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said: By God!
Rav Huna said:
Even impurity and then impurity again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing version of the same רב הונא statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר is liable separately even for a second impurity.

steps.title: Proof: the נזיר in the cemetery who touches a body
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cites another ruling of רב הונא: a נזיר standing in a cemetery who touches a dead body handed to him is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב הונא said: A נזיר who was standing in a cemetery, and they handed him his dead relative or another dead body, and he touched it, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a known ruling of רב הונא to back up his version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר standing in a cemetery is already impure. Yet רב הונא says he is liable for touching another body. This sets up the argument in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Cemetery
They handed him / held out to him
Liable (here, to lashes)

phrases.english: For Rav Huna said:
A nazir who was standing in a cemetery,
and they handed him his dead relative, or another dead body,
and he touched it: he is liable.

steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's version of רב הונא (liable even for impurity twice)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling about a נזיר in a cemetery

steps.title: He was already impure, so רב הונא must hold impurity twice counts
steps.stepSummary: Since the נזיר in the cemetery was already impure and is still liable, רב הונא must hold that a second impurity brings separate liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he liable? He is already impure and standing that way! Rather, isn't it clear from here that רב הונא said: even impurity and then impurity again?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף draws the conclusion from the cemetery case and wraps up his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question "why is he liable?" is not a real doubt. It shows that the only way to explain the ruling is that a second impurity counts. That confirms רב יוסף's version over רבה's.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
He is already impure and stays that way
Rather, isn't it clear to learn from this

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's proof: a נזיר who is already impure (in a cemetery) is still liable for touching a body, so a second impurity counts.

phrases.english: Why?
He is already impure and stands that way!
Rather, isn't it clear to learn from this
that Rav Huna said:
even impurity and then impurity again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? הָא מִיטַּמֵּא וְקָאֵים! אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the case in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא holds a נזיר is liable even for impurity on top of impurity.

steps.title: אביי objects from the כהן holding a dead body
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a ברייתא: a כהן already carrying a dead body who touches another is not liable, because the verse speaks only of one who is not yet profaned.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: A כהן who had a dead body resting on his shoulder, and they handed him his dead relative or another dead body, and he touched it, you might think he is liable. So the verse says "and he shall not profane": this applies to someone who is not yet profaned. That excludes this one, who is already profaned and stays that way.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף with a ברייתא that seems to say a second impurity does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case closely matches רב הונא's cemetery case: someone already impure touches another body. Here the ruling is not liable, based on "ולא יחלל." That goes against רב יוסף's idea that a second impurity brings new liability.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think
Therefore the verse says
And he shall not profane
Already profaned and stays that way

phrases.english: Abaye challenged him:
A kohen who had a dead body
resting on his shoulder,
and they handed him his dead relative, or another dead body,
and he touched it: you might think he should be liable.
So the verse says: "And he shall not profane,"
meaning someone who is not yet profaned,
which excludes this one, who is already profaned and stays that way.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that a second impurity brings separate liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says someone already impure ("profaned") is not liable for touching another body, so a second impurity should not count.

steps.title: רב יוסף pushes back: the משנה then troubles you
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that אביי's reading clashes with our משנה, which makes a נזיר liable for each warning even though he is already impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then let our משנה be difficult for you! For we learned: If he kept becoming impure from dead bodies all day, he is liable only once. If people told him "Don't become impure, don't become impure," he is liable for each and every time. But why? He is already impure and stays that way!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends himself by showing that אביי's position runs into trouble with our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a נזיר warned again and again is liable for each impurity, even though after the first one he is already impure. So the משנה seems to agree that a second impurity counts. רב יוסף is saying the problem is not only his: אביי must also explain this משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let it be difficult for you
Do not become impure: a warning given before the sin
For each and every one

steps.confusionAlert: Lashes need a warning before the sin. That is why many impurities with one warning bring one set of lashes, while each new warning brings another set.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Then let our mishnah be difficult for you!
For we learned:
If he kept becoming impure from dead bodies all day,
he is liable only once.
If they told him "Don't become impure, don't become impure,"
he is liable for each and every one.
But why?
He is already impure and stays that way!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge with a counter-challenge from the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's position that a second impurity brings no new liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes a נזיר liable for each warned impurity even though he is already impure, which seems to contradict the idea behind "מחולל ועומד."

steps.title: The משנה and the ברייתא clash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that the משנה and the ברייתא really do seem to contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the two sources contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: After seeing that the ברייתא clashes with our משנה, the גמרא states the problem openly: the two sources contradict each other. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that someone already impure from a dead body is not liable for touching another one. The משנה says a נזיר who is already impure is still liable for each new contact. Both cannot be true in the same case, so the גמרא needs to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty or contradiction
With each other (one source against the other)

phrases.english: Rather, they are difficult against each other!
phrases.notes: 'They' means our משנה and the ברייתא אביי quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב יוסף's point that אביי's ברייתא clashes with the משנה, and states the contradiction outright.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא (no liability for a second impurity) set against the משנה (liability for each warning while impure).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two authoritative sources give opposite rulings on impurity on top of impurity, so one seems to be wrong unless they can be told apart.

steps.title: Still touching the first body versus already let go
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about someone still touching the first body. The משנה is about someone who let go before touching the next one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it means connected contact; there it means contact that is not connected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the person is still holding the first body when he touches the second, so the second touch adds nothing new and brings no liability. In the משנה, he separated from the first body before touching again, so each new contact is a fresh impurity and brings its own liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Connected contact: still touching the source of impurity
Not connected: he already separated from the first source
It is not a difficulty (start of an answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch which כָּאן is which. The first 'here' (connected) is the ברייתא, where he is not liable. The second 'here' (not connected) is the משנה, where he is liable.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
Here, it is with connected contact.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא: he is still holding the first body when he touches the second.

phrases.english: There, it is without connected contact.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן — בְּחִיבּוּרִין. כָּאן — שֶׁלֹּא בְּחִיבּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and ברייתא seemed to be talking about the same case and disagreeing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about connected contact (no new liability). The משנה is about separate contacts (new liability each time).

steps.title: Is connected impurity really a rule from the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: רבי ינאי taught that connected impurity applies only to תרומה and קדשים, not to a נזיר or someone bringing the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is connected impurity a rule from the תורה? But רב יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי ינאי: They said connected impurity only for תרומה and holy foods, but not for a נזיר or one making the פסח. If it were from the תורה, why would there be a difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. Does 'connected contact' really carry weight in the eyes of the תורה, especially for a נזיר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 8 treats being connected to impurity as a real תורה-level fact. But רבי ינאי says the connected-impurity rule does not apply to a נזיר at all, only to תרומה and קדשים. A limit like that suggests it is only a rule of the חכמים, since a תורה rule would apply equally everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: From the תורה (not just a rabbinic rule)
The כהן's portion and holy sacrificial foods
One who brings the קרבן פסח
What is the difference?

phrases.english: And is connected impurity from the Torah?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef say
that Rabbi Yannai said:
They did not state connected impurity
except for teruma and holy foods,
but for a nazir and one who makes the Pesach offering, no.
And if you say it is from the Torah, what is the difference?
phrases.notes: If the תורה made the rule, it should apply to a נזיר just as it does to תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוּמְאָה בְּחִיבּוּרִין דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא? הָא אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that connected impurity determines a נזיר's liability.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ינאי limits connected impurity to תרומה and קדשים and excludes a נזיר, so the rule must be rabbinic. If so, it cannot change a נזיר's תורה-level liability.

steps.title: Person-to-person versus person-to-body
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי was talking about a person touching another person who is touching a dead body. Our case is a person touching the dead body directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, it is a person connected to a person. There, it is a person connected to a dead body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying there are two kinds of 'connected' impurity, and רבי ינאי was only talking about one of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ינאי's rabbinic-level rule is about a chain: someone touches a person who is touching a body. Our case is a person directly holding a body. That is a real תורה-level connection, so it can affect a נזיר's liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Connected through another person
Directly connected to a dead body

phrases.english: Here, it is a person connected to a person.
phrases.notes: This is רבי ינאי's case, where the impurity comes through another person.

phrases.english: There, it is a person connected to a dead body.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּאן, בְּחִיבּוּרֵי אָדָם בְּאָדָם. כָּאן, בְּחִיבּוּרֵי אָדָם בְּמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי ינאי in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: two different kinds of connection.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All connected impurity seemed to be only rabbinic.
steps.terutzMaskana: Connection through a person is rabbinic. Direct connection to a dead body is from the תורה and applies to a נזיר.

steps.title: No new liability for impurity on top of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that while someone is still touching a body, a second impurity brings no new liability, because he is already impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But impurity on top of impurity, no, because he is already standing in his impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up the result. If he is still connected to the first body, touching another body does not make him liable again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second contact adds nothing, since he is right now in the middle of being made impure. This matches רבה's ruling, which this סוגיא has been working toward: separate contacts can bring separate liability, but impurity on top of impurity while still connected does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity on top of impurity
He is already impure and stays in that state

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר who separates from one dead body and then touches another is liable again. But if he is still holding the first body, the second touch brings no new liability. This is because direct connection to a body counts on a תורה level, unlike connection through another person.

phrases.english: But impurity on top of impurity, no,
since he is already impure and standing that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל טוּמְאָה וְטוּמְאָה לָא, דְּהָא מִיטַּמֵּא וְקָאֵים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final ruling from the answers in steps 8 and 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Impurity on top of impurity, while still directly connected to a dead body, does not create new liability, because the person is already standing in his impurity.

steps.title: Shouldn't the same logic cancel the extra punishment for entering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the rule from step 11 to the case of טומאה וביאה. A person entering a covered place with a dead body is already impure, so why should he get an extra punishment for entering?
steps.simpleTranslation: The same should be true of impurity and entering: he is already impure and standing that way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the conclusion it just reached and uses it to challenge a different ruling, the extra punishment a נזיר gets for entering a place with a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said that a second impurity brings no new liability for someone who is already impure. But רב הונא's ruling, as רבה reported it in step 1, gives separate lashes for impurity and for entering. If the נזיר is already impure when he enters, the same logic says the entering should add nothing, so why the extra lashes?

keyTerms.meaning: Becoming impure and entering: a נזיר who goes into a covered place that has a dead body in it
Also, likewise
He is already impure and standing that way, so nothing new happens to him

phrases.english: Impurity and entering, likewise,
phrases.notes: This is the case where a נזיר is punished both for becoming impure and for entering a covered place with a dead body.

phrases.english: he is already impure and standing that way!

steps.triggerLanguage: טוּמְאָה וּבִיאָה נָמֵי, הָא מִיטַּמֵּא וְקָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusion of step 11 to attack the double punishment for טומאה וביאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a נזיר gets separate punishments for becoming impure and for entering a place with a dead body.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If someone already impure gets no new punishment for a second impurity, then a נזיר who is already impure when he enters should get no new punishment for entering either.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a house is different from a field
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the double punishment applies when a pure person walks into a house with a body. If he became impure in a field first and then entered, the entering adds nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Here it is talking about a house; there it is talking about a field.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge by splitting the case into two situations: one where the punishment for entering applies and one where it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the house case the person was pure, and walking in made him impure and broke the rule against entering at the same moment, so he gets two punishments. In the field case he already became impure by touching a body outside, so when he later enters while still touching it, he is 'already impure' and the entering brings no new punishment. Step 11's rule stays true, but it only covers the field case.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there: the גמרא's way of saying two rulings are about two different cases
House, a covered place where the dead body is
Field, an open place where he became impure before entering

steps.whatToRemember: Entering a place with a dead body adds a separate punishment only when the impurity and the entering happen together, as when a pure נזיר walks into a house. If he was already impure from a field, entering adds nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the field case means entering is never punished. The entering is the same act, but he gets no new punishment because he was already impure before he walked in.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Here, it is talking about a house,
phrases.notes: This is the ruling of two punishments. He was pure, walked in, and became impure at the same moment he entered.

phrases.english: there, it is talking about a field.
phrases.notes: He touched a body in a field first, then entered while still touching it, so there is no new punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כָּאן בְּבַיִת, כָּאן בְּשָׂדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 by separating two cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ruling applies to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought every entering happens after the person is already impure, so it can never add a punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: When a pure person enters a house with a body, impurity and entering happen at once, so he gets two punishments. When he was already impure from a field, entering adds nothing.
